title: Why Does My Home Feel Humid Even When the AC Is Running? - Rosenberg Plumbing & Air
desc: Your AC helps remove humidity in the summer. If your home is still sticky, your AC may be short-cycling. Look for these signs to call for repair.

blocks.text: In San Antonio, TX, a powerful air conditioner is a necessity. But what happens when your AC cools the air, yet your home still feels damp, sticky, and uncomfortable? This is a common issue for homeowners during our long and humid cooling season. While your AC is running and the thermostat says it’s cool, you might still notice clammy air, musty odors, condensation on windows, or a general feeling of uneven comfort.

This frustrating situation often points to an underlying issue with your HVAC system. An air conditioner’s job is to remove excess moisture from the air while cooling the house. When it fails to do this effectively, your home can feel uncomfortably humid. This problem can stem from several sources, including incorrect system operation, poor airflow, maintenance needs, or even improper equipment sizing.
Why Your Home Can Feel Humid With the AC On

Cooling and dehumidifying are two distinct processes. As your air conditioner runs, warm, moist indoor air passes over the cold evaporator coil. This process cools the air, and as a byproduct, water vapor condenses on the coil and drains away, reducing humidity.

However, this dehumidification process works only when the AC runs long enough. If the system runs only in short bursts, it may cool the air to the set temperature without running long enough to remove a significant amount of moisture. Poor airflow can also hinder the evaporator coil’s ability to pull moisture from the air. When combined with the high outdoor humidity common in San Antonio, these factors can leave your home feeling cool but damp.
Your AC May Be Short-Cycling

One of the most common culprits behind a humid home is short-cycling. This occurs when your air conditioner turns on and off too frequently, running for just a few minutes at a time. While the system may succeed in quickly lowering the air temperature, these brief cycles are not long enough for effective dehumidification.

The primary cause of short-cycling is often an oversized air conditioner. A system that is too powerful for your home will cool the space so rapidly that it satisfies the thermostat and shuts off before it can remove adequate moisture. Thermostat issues, such as incorrect placement in direct sunlight or near a heat source, can also cause false readings and lead to short cycles. Beyond creating a humid environment, short cycling puts excessive wear and tear on your AC’s components, leading to premature breakdowns and higher energy bills.
Poor Airflow Can Limit Dehumidification

Proper airflow is essential for your air conditioner to effectively cool and dehumidify your home. Air needs to move freely across the evaporator coil for condensation and moisture removal. With restricted airflow, the system’s performance suffers, and humidity levels can rise.
Several issues can lead to poor airflow, which a professional can address. Identifying the source of the blockage is the first step toward restoring comfort and efficiency to your home.

A lack of routine system care is often the root cause of these problems. During regular AC maintenance, a technician cleans coils, inspects motors, and changes filters if necessary, preventing airflow issues that could impact your comfort.
The AC System May Be the Wrong Size

The size of your air conditioner must match your home’s unique cooling needs. An oversized unit will short cycle, failing to remove humidity. An undersized unit will run constantly, struggling to cool your home and unable to keep up with the moisture load on hot, humid San Antonio days.

Your home’s cooling requirements can also change over time. Recent renovations, new windows, or a home addition can alter the original calculation. If you suspect your AC is the wrong size, a professional HVAC technician can perform a detailed load calculation. This assessment considers factors like square footage, insulation levels, window placement, and local climate to determine the exact size and capacity your home requires for optimal cooling and dehumidification.
Thermostat and Fan Settings Could Be Contributing

Sometimes, the solution to a humid home is as simple as adjusting your thermostat settings. Many homeowners set their thermostat to On instead of Auto. While the On setting provides constant air circulation, it can also reintroduce moisture into your home. After a cooling cycle ends, the continuously running fan can blow moisture sitting on the indoor coil back into your living space.

When you set the fan to Auto, it will run only when the AC is actively cooling. This allows the collected moisture to drain away properly. Additionally, the location of your thermostat can impact system performance. If it’s in an area that gets unusually hot or cold, it can give inaccurate readings. You may also need to review smart thermostat settings and optimize them for humidity control.
When a Whole-House Dehumidifier Can Help

For some homes in San Antonio, especially those with persistent moisture concerns, an air conditioner alone may not be enough to achieve ideal humidity levels. In these cases, a whole-house dehumidifier is an excellent solution. This system integrates directly with your existing HVAC system to manage humidity throughout your entire home.

A whole-house dehumidifier works alongside your air conditioner, removing excess moisture from the air independently. This allows you to feel more comfortable at a slightly higher thermostat setting, which can help you save on energy costs. By effectively controlling indoor humidity, these systems can also help reduce musty odors and create a healthier indoor environment. Professional sizing and installation are crucial to ensure the dehumidifier meets your home’s specific needs.
Signs You Should Schedule HVAC Service

If you’ve tried adjusting your thermostat settings and your home still feels humid, it’s time to call a professional. A trained technician can diagnose the root cause of the problem and recommend the right solution.
These issues rarely resolve on their own and can worsen over time, leading to more complex problems. If you’re noticing any of these signs, schedule professional AC repair.
